- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained or gradual mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes, model underreacts — forecasts remain high while true values decline more aggressively.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward higher values, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Forecasts often fail to capture downward momentum in the latter half of the 30-day window.
- Model underestimates true price declines during periods of strong downward pressure.
- Forecasts show persistent lag in adjusting to recent price drops — often taking 3–5 days to correct.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility, leading to exaggerated peaks and troughs.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — forecasts stay too far from historical averages for extended periods.
- Model tends to ignore long-term trend direction, especially when prices are trending downward.
